title: First Commit to Production - Hosted API hypotheses and quickstart hooks
summary: Working draft: short, developer-centric messaging AND a set of quickstart copy + pricing language experiments aimed at driving first successful production call (MVP -> production). Includes competitive callouts and suggested A/B buckets.
body:
Purpose:
- Capture a tight, developer-first set of hooks that move an engineer from opening the docs to shipping a production call (the ‘first commit’ moment).
- Surface simple pricing language that reduces friction for experimentation and enterprise conversion.
- Propose lightweight A/B experiments for copy and funnel measurement.

Context / problem we solve:
- Developers evaluate dozens of APIs; most drop off because they can’t get a predictable latency/cost read or can’t run a sample in their stack quickly.
- Our advantage: consistent performance across hosted/dedicated/private and a concise set of levers (batching, cache, quantization). Need messaging that highlights fast time-to-confident-call and cost clarity.

Primary persona(s):
- Backend engineer at a growth-stage SaaS startup (primary): needs <100ms p95 for synchronous features and predictable token cost.
- Platform engineer at mid-market (secondary): needs policy/routing and audit controls.
- Prototype/power-user (tertiary): tries different models and cares about quick iteration.

Core developer-first value props (short bullets / one-liners to test):
1) "Call in minutes, scale with predictable latency" — emphasize fast onboarding + p95 SLOs and routing fallbacks.
2) "Transparent token economics you can simulate locally" — simple per-token pricing example + cost estimator.
3) "Same API across hosted, dedicated, and private" — removes refactor risk when moving to enterprise.
4) "Turn on batching & cache suggestions to shave costs without sacrificing latency" — concrete example showing 30% cost improvement.

Quickstart angle drafts (3 variants to A/B test on the landing + onboarding email):
A. Minimal friction "Hello World" developer hook (A: copy-focused)
- Headline: "First call in under 5 minutes"
- Subhead: "Generate text, chat, or embeddings from a single REST call. No infra, no config."
- CTA: "Try a 1-minute demo + free credits"
- Quickstart steps (1-3 lines each): 1) Sign up and paste your API key, 2) Run curl example, 3) Add SDK and deploy.
- Success metric: % of new signups who make 1st API call within 10 minutes.

B. Predictable-cost-first (B: cost-focused)
- Headline: "Know the cost before you build"
- Subhead: "Estimate requests, preview token usage, and pick a model profile for predictable unit economics."
- CTA: "Open cost estimator"
- Quickstart change: include an inline cost-estimate snippet showing cost per 1k tokens for common models.
- Success metric: click-through to estimator and signups who run estimator.

C. Migration-safe promise (C: lock-in/enterprise angle)
- Headline: "Build once, run anywhere"
- Subhead: "Same API and rollout controls from hosted prototypes to dedicated clusters and private VPCs."
- CTA: "See migration checklist"
- Quickstart change: include a one-page migration checklist and sample rollout config.
- Success metric: inbound demo requests from platform teams.

Pricing language drafts (simple phrasing to test in UI, docs, and sign-up flows):
- Option 1 (developer-friendly simple): "Pay as you go. 0.8¢ per 1k tokens for generation; 0.2¢ per 1k tokens for embeddings. Free $25 credit for new dev accounts."
- Option 2 (transparency + estimator): "Per-token pricing with an on-page cost estimator — see your monthly spend for 100k/1M requests. Discounts auto-apply as usage grows."
- Option 3 (commit-first gating for enterprise): "Start with hosted API, upgrade to Dedicated with predictable monthly commit. Contact sales for custom pricing and migration support."
- Microcopy notes: avoid ambiguous words like 'cheap' or 'unlimited'. Use explicit units (tokens/1k tokens/month) and show example invoice lines.

Callouts and competitive notes (short):
- Compared to big cloud AI endpoints: they emphasize model access but often leave out per-request latency guarantees and clear migration paths. We should call out: predictable latency, rollout controls, and unified API across environments.
- Compared to simple-hosted LLM APIs: our differentiator is the migration story + tooling for cost control (batching suggestions, cache).
- Risks: Be careful not to overpromise latency for every model/size; show benchmark ranges and point to model-profiles.

Suggested experiments / measurement plan (quick):
- Experiment 1: Landing page headline A vs B vs C (see above). Metric: 7-day funnel conversion from page view -> signup -> 1st API call.
- Experiment 2: Pricing microcopy (Option 1 vs Option 2) on sign-up. Metric: trial activation rate and 30-day retention.
- Experiment 3: Quickstart CTA placement (code-first vs estimator-first). Metric: time-to-first-production-call and support touch rate.

Onboarding checklist for engineering flow (to include in quickstart):
1) Create API key and paste into local env (example command).
2) Run curated curl example for generation (with model-profile param).
3) Run embedded cost estimator locally (example snippet with expected tokens).
4) Add SDK and call from simple serverless function.
5) Enable basic SLO alerting and cost threshold in Console.

Sample short-form copy snippets for use in small banners / CTAs:
- "Make your first generation call in minutes — free credits included."
- "Estimate cost for your workload — see exact token math."
- "Migrate to Dedicated without changing code."

Open questions / parking-lot items:
- What is the canonical wording for 'token' in customer-facing copy? (token vs token-unit vs token-credit) recommend: 'token' but always show 'per 1k tokens' for clarity.
- Do we offer prepackaged examples for common frameworks (Express, Rails, Flask, Next.js)? (should be yes; track PRs).
- Which model-profiles should be surfaced in quickstart (small, med, large) with benchmarked p95 latency samples? Need input from serving-runtime and bench team. See ticket JIRA-RUN-229.
- How do we measure 'first production commit'? instrumenting a combination of: first SDK install + first key used in non-localhost environment + tagging from Console. Ops: GTM-analytics to own.

Appendix: example API copy (curl) to include in quickstart (two-line example for minimal friction):
- curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -d '{"model":"rwd-small-1","input":"Summarize the following: ..."}'
- (Add snippet showing the token-total header and cost calculation)

Next steps (owners / immediate actions):
- Iterate headline variants with design and wire up variant landing pages (owner: Asha) - deadline: 2026-02-28.
- Get model p95 samples from serving-runtime for the three model-profiles we plan to ship examples for (owner: Riley) - ticket: JIRA-RUN-229.
- Draft pricing page microcopy and build a tiny on-page estimator (owner: Miguel) - PR #128 referenced above.

Notes to self and quick brain-dump (rough):
- Keep language action-oriented and time-to-value oriented (minutes, p95, cost/1k).
- Developers respond to short runnable examples; put a minimal cURL + SDK example above the fold.
- Make cost examples concrete: "3 calls/minute for a month = $X" beats abstractions.
- Slack thread: #gtm-hosted-api for rapid review.

References / links:
- Confluence draft (long-form): https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/CONF-1742-first-commit-hosted-api
- Internal experiment dashboard (GTM analytics): GA-DASH-05 (private)
- Quickstarts repo PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quickstarts/pull/128

End.
